candidates.change_summary: Return a different bytes4 value (0x12345678) instead of the onERC721Received selector.
Delete the return statement so the function returns the default value 0.
Return the ERC165 supportsInterface selector constant instead of the onERC721Received selector.
Replace the assignment `baseToken = _baseToken;` with `baseToken = address(0);` so baseToken always reads as zero after initialization.
Replace the assignment `baseToken = _baseToken;` with `baseToken = _nft;` so baseToken is set to the NFT address instead.
Delete the statement `baseToken = _baseToken;` so baseToken remains address(0) after initialization.
Remove the statement `nft = _nft;` so the pool's `nft` state variable is never set and remains address(0).
Replace `nft = _nft;` with `nft = address(0);` so `nft()` always returns the zero address after initialization.
Replace `nft = _nft;` with `nft = _baseToken;` so the pool's `nft` state variable is set to the base token address instead.
Delete the assignment `changeFee = _changeFee;` so changeFee remains 0 after initialize.
Replace `changeFee = _changeFee;` with `changeFee = uint56(_feeRate);` so changeFee is set from the feeRate parameter instead.
Replace `changeFee = _changeFee;` with `changeFee = _changeFee + 1;` so the stored changeFee is one larger than the argument for any non-maximal input.
Delete the statement `feeRate = _feeRate;` so feeRate remains its default value instead of the caller-supplied value.
Replace `feeRate = _feeRate;` with `feeRate = 1;` so feeRate is set to 1 regardless of the supplied value.
Replace `feeRate = _feeRate;` with `feeRate = _feeRate + 1;` so the stored feeRate is one greater than the supplied value (valid since _feeRate <= 5000).
Change the bounds check from `_feeRate > 5_000` to `_feeRate >= 5_000` so that initializing with feeRate of exactly 5000 now reverts instead of storing 5000.
